The study empirically supports the exact claim made: detectors flagged TOEFL (non-native) essays as AI-generated at an average false-positive rate of 61.22% while accuracy on native US 8th-grade essays was near-perfect, and the bias is tied to lexical/linguistic features (perplexity), not actual AI use.

sources.cite: Liang, W., Yuksekgonul, M., Mao, Y., Wu, E., & Zou, J. (2023). GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers. Patterns, 4(7), 100779.
sources.finding: Across seven widely-used GPT detectors, non-native-authored TOEFL essays were misclassified as AI-generated at an average false-positive rate of 61.22%, while detectors were near-perfect (essentially 0% false positives) on native-speaker US 8th-grade essays; 97.8% of TOEFL essays were flagged by at least one detector. Enriching TOEFL word choice cut false positives to 11.77%, confirming the bias tracks linguistic features, not AI use. Peer-reviewed, Cell Press, canonical for this claim.
